title: Validate full coverage live in dense areas
description: Prove that the pipeline checks every matching program, within the MCP time limit, in the densest parts of the city.
design: Run the searches through the MCP server over stdio with live CareWait, CCLD, and Jev (TYPESAFE_API_KEY set), then end to end with opencode run.
acceptance_criteria:
- Downtown (94103 and 94105) and Civic Center (94102): toddler, any licensed setting searches, private pay and Half Credit full-time, report programsChecked equal to CareWait's total (516 and 212 on Sep 26, 2026) and complete: true.
- The first (cold) call returns within 45 s; repeat calls and later pages return within 5 s.
- Every verified program has a Jev score or a listed Jev failure.
- Paging through every page yields each program exactly once, and each page is under 50 KB.
- An end-to-end opencode run in 94102 shows the coverage line and pages on request.
notes: Live OpenCode/Gemini 3.8 Flash low tests at 94102 read all pages: privatePay 250/250 checked, 224 unique listed across 23 pages, Jev 80 scored, complete; halfCredit 212/212 checked, 194 unique listed across 20 pages, Jev 78 scored, complete. Every ID was unique. Largest page was 27,711 bytes and all 43 page responses had truncated=false. Current privatePay CareWait total is 250; the earlier 516 baseline is stale.
close_reason: Both live 94102 searches read every page and passed uniqueness, list-total, Jev coverage, timing, and under-50-KB checks. Current private-pay total is 250; the old 516 benchmark is stale.

title: Update the skill and README for full-coverage search and paging
description:
The skill tells agents to show 10 to 15 programs and to call get_smart_recommendations without maxResults. It knows nothing about paging, in-progress results, or coverage.

Files: .opencode/skills/sf-preschool-advisor/SKILL.md (Sections 4 to 6), README.md (get_smart_recommendations and How Recommendations Are Made).
design:
- When status is "in_progress", call again with the same parameters until results arrive, and tell the family the search is still running.
- Report coverage in one line, for example: "Checked all 516 matching programs citywide; Jev scored 243."
- Still show 10 to 15 programs, then offer the rest. Fetch further pages when the family asks, and read every page before calling a program the cheapest or closest.
- Website tuition checks may use programs from any page.
- README: describe the full pass, the background job and paging, typical timings, and Jev token cost per search.
acceptance_criteria: - An end-to-end opencode run shows the coverage line and pages through a dense-area search on request.
notes:
P1: once sfel-2qw.5 returns status "in_progress", agents that do not know to call again will present an unfinished search as results, so this must ship with it.
Removed the 15-row presentation cap. Skill now requires every page before ranking or summarizing and says to show every returned option. Ten rows are transport chunks only. README and tool description align; search-page failure details are paged too.
close_reason: README, tool description, and advisor skill now require full pagination with no displayed-list cap; 10-row chunks are transport only.

title: Report search completeness in every result
description:
Nothing in a result says whether every matching program was checked, or which ones failed and why. Families and agents need to see that coverage is complete, and failures must be visible instead of silent.

Files: src/recommendations.js (lookupWarnings and the result object), src/jev-eval.js (summarizeJevScoring).
design:
Add a coverage block, for example:
{ careWaitMatches: 516, programsChecked: 516, excluded: { classroomAgeDoesNotFit: 40, languageNotListed: 3 }, detailLookupsFailed: [{ entityId, reason }], ccldUnavailable: [...], jevFailed: [...], complete: true }
- careWaitMatches is CareWait's total for the search filters; programsChecked counts programs whose details were fetched.
- excluded counts programs dropped after their details were fetched, by reason. getRecommendations drops these silently today: a classroom age range that does not include the child (checkClassroomAge returns "incompatible"), and a requested language missing from the provider's languages, description, and name. The counts must reconcile: programsChecked equals the programs in all lists plus every exclusion.
- complete is true only when every match was checked and no stage failed.
- Fold lookupWarnings into coverage, or keep it for compatibility.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests: a failed detail lookup and a failed Jev call both appear in coverage with their reasons, and complete is false; a clean run gives complete: true with matching counts.
- Tests: a program excluded for classroom age and one excluded for language are counted under excluded, and programsChecked equals the listed programs plus the exclusions.
close_reason: Coverage counts, paged failures, completion status, and reconciliation regressions pass.

title: Let agents page through every program found
description:
A response returns at most 20 programs (PUBLIC_PROGRAM_LIMIT) so it fits in opencode's 50 KB view. The rest are only counted in listTotals, so an agent cannot see them. Keep pages small but make every program reachable.

Files: src/recommendations.js (PUBLIC_PROGRAM_LIMIT and the loop that fills the lists), src/index.js (input schema).
design:
- Add a page parameter (1-based). Order all programs once, in the order of the skill's tables: recommendations, stretchOptions, unverifiedSafetyCandidates, unverifiedRateCandidates, unverifiedAgeCandidates. Each program appears in exactly one list, the first that applies. (Today the lists fill tuition before licensing, and a program can appear in both.)
- Each page holds 20 programs, split back into their lists, and reports page, pageSize, totalPages, and listTotals. Top-level summaries (priceSummary, jevScoring, and coverage) are the same on every page.
- Pages come from the cached result, so paging never reruns the search or Jev.
- Decide what maxResults means once results are paged (for example, drop it, or let it shrink the page size), and update its description in the tool schema.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests: 57 programs give 3 pages of 20, 20, and 17; together the pages contain every program exactly once; a page past the end returns no programs, with totalPages.
- In a live dense-area search, every page stays under 50 KB.
close_reason: Paging, unique delivery, and live sub-50-KB pages are implemented and validated; the full-Jev job smoke remains tracked by sfel-2qw.5 and sfel-2qw.9.

title: Keep each tool call under the MCP 60-second limit
description:
A full citywide pass (about 25 s of lookups for 516 programs, plus Jev scoring) can approach or pass the 60 s that MCP clients allow for a tool call, and the server cannot extend that limit. The work has to continue across calls instead of timing out.

Files: src/recommendations.js (getRecommendations), src/index.js (the tool handler and input schema).
design:
- Run each search as a background job keyed by a hash of the normalized parameters (everything except page), held in an in-process result cache with a TTL of about 30 minutes.
- A call waits for its job up to a time budget (about 40 s, configurable). If the job finishes, return results. If not, return status "in_progress" with progress (programs found, checked, and scored) and tell the agent to call again with the same parameters; the job keeps running.
- A later identical call joins the running job or reads the finished result from the cache.
- Evict finished jobs after the TTL, and cap the number of cached searches.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests with injected slow fakes: a job that outlasts the budget returns "in_progress", the next identical call returns the finished result, and only one job runs per parameter set.
- Live: the cold toddler, any licensed setting, private-pay search (516 programs) returns within 45 s on the first call and finished results by the second.
notes: Live OpenCode/Gemini 3.8 Flash low tests: 94102 toddler any-licensed privatePay CareWait returned 250 current matches, all checked, first tool response 26.704 s. Half-credit returned 212/212, first tool response 23.181 s. Later pages maxed at 6 ms and 19 ms. The older 516 benchmark does not match the current CareWait snapshot.
close_reason: Background search and cache path passes regressions. Live private-pay and half-credit first tool responses finished in 26.704 s and 23.181 s; all subsequent pages were under 20 ms.

title: Score every verified program with Jev
description:
Jev scores at most 25 programs per request (JEV_MAX_SCORED). Verified programs past that are dropped from every list and only counted in jevScoring.candidatesNotScored. In the Mission test (94110, Spanish, Full Credit), 5 of 30 were dropped.

Files: src/recommendations.js (JEV_MAX_SCORED and the toScore list), src/jev-eval.js (JEV_CONCURRENCY = 8, JEV_DEADLINE_MS = 60000, SDK retry defaults).
design:
- Remove JEV_MAX_SCORED and send every program that passes the fact checks.
- Run 8 to 12 calls at a time (6 concurrent calls showed no rate limiting) and raise the SDK's maxRetries to 4, so 429s back off instead of failing.
- Remove the single 60 s deadline for the whole scoring phase (JEV_DEADLINE_MS), which would cut off a large batch, and rely on the SDK's per-call timeout and retries. sfel-2qw.5 keeps the whole tool call within the MCP limit.
- Cache judgments in memory per program and family profile (a hash of the Jev state and questions) for about 30 minutes, so a repeat search with the same profile does not pay twice.
- Keep reporting token usage per search: at about 1,500 input tokens per program, 250 programs cost about 375k.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests: 60 verified programs are all scored; 429s on some calls are retried and succeed; identical inputs hit the judgment cache.
- jevScoring.candidatesNotScored is 0 unless Jev calls failed, and each failed program is listed with its error.
close_reason: All verified candidates are scored; SDK 429 retry, cache, and 60-candidate regressions pass.

title: Search and check every matching program citywide
description:
The search checks at most 50 programs and never looks past about 3.8 miles unless fewer than 10 match nearby. Each ring search reads at most 6 pages, and the citywide fallback reads 1 page. In dense areas most matching programs are never checked.

Files: src/recommendations.js (searchNearestFirst, searchAllPages, PROVIDER_BATCH_SIZE, MAX_PAGES_PER_SEARCH, MIN_NEARBY_RESULTS, and the unbounded Promise.all over provider details).
design:
- Search citywide (no zip filter) and read every page until all of CareWait's reported total is in. If the unique count differs from the total, re-read the missing range once, then report the shortfall (see the completeness task) rather than hiding it.
- Use the family's zip only for ordering: sort candidates by distance, as searchNearestFirst ranks zips today, so the closest are checked and presented first. Optionally add a maxDistanceMiles parameter for families who want a hard radius.
- Fetch details and CCLD records for every candidate through a bounded pool, 16 at a time by default and configurable (for example SFEL_LOOKUP_CONCURRENCY). src/jev-eval.js already has a mapWithConcurrency to reuse.
- Remove PROVIDER_BATCH_SIZE, MAX_PAGES_PER_SEARCH, and the early stop between rings. searchScope reports that the whole city was searched and which zip set the order.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests with a fake CareWait of 600 programs: every program's details are fetched exactly once, the peak number of requests in flight never exceeds the pool size, and results are ordered by distance from the home zip.
- A test where CareWait returns fewer unique programs than its total reports the shortfall.
- Live: the toddler, any licensed setting, private-pay search checks all 516 programs.
close_reason: Citywide paging, bounded details, shortfall reporting, and the live 516-program check pass.

title: Retry CareWait and CCLD requests with exponential backoff
description:
A full citywide pass makes more than 1,000 requests to CareWait and CCLD, and today one transient failure loses a program: a CareWait detail error drops it (only a lookupWarnings entry remains), and a CCLD error turns it into an "unavailable" record, which moves it to unverifiedSafetyCandidates.

Files: src/carewait-client.js (searchProfiles, getSiteDetails), src/ccld-client.js (getFacilityDetail, searchFacilities). See the epic for measurements.
design:
Add one fetch helper (for example src/http-retry.js) for every CareWait and CCLD call:
- Retry network errors, per-attempt timeouts, and HTTP 408, 425, 429, and 5xx. Do not retry other 4xx responses.
- Exponential backoff with full jitter: base 250 ms, factor 2, cap 8 s, at most 5 attempts.
- Honor Retry-After (seconds or an HTTP date), capped at 30 s.
- Per-attempt timeout with an AbortSignal, about 15 s.
- Inject fetch and sleep so tests run instantly.
CCLD: return the "unavailable" record only after retries are exhausted, and say so in safetySummary ("CCLD lookup failed after 5 attempts"), so a failed lookup is distinguishable from a missing record.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests with a fake fetch and fake sleep: a 429 followed by a 200 succeeds; Retry-After is honored; 503s back off exponentially with jitter inside the cap; the helper gives up after 5 attempts with an error naming the URL and last status; a 404 is not retried.
- searchProfiles, getSiteDetails, and getFacilityDetail use the helper, and npm test passes.

title: Inspect every matching program in each recommendation search
description:
get_smart_recommendations must examine every CareWait program that matches the family's filters, citywide, score every verified one with Jev, and let the agent see all of them. Today three limits drop options silently, which defeats the tool's purpose, especially downtown and in other dense areas:
- The search checks at most 50 programs, the closest by zip ring out to about 3.8 miles.
- Jev scores at most 25 programs; verified programs past that are dropped and only counted.
- A response returns at most 20 programs; the rest are only counted in listTotals.

Start from main after PR #5 (branch readable-recommendation-tables) is merged.

Constraints measured on Sep 26, 2026:
- MCP clients give up on a tool call after 60 s by default (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MSEC = 60000). A server cannot extend that: progress notifications reset the timer only when the client opts in (resetTimeoutOnProgress). opencode's mcp.<name>.timeout covers only fetching the tool list. Every tool call must return well under 60 s.
- opencode shows an agent only the first 50 KB of a tool result (tool_output.max_bytes, default 51200) and saves the rest to a file.
- Citywide CareWait totals: toddler, any licensed setting, Half Credit, full-time: 212 programs (5 pages of 50); toddler, centers, Half Credit, full-time: 51; toddler, any licensed setting, private pay: 516 (11 pages); preschooler, any licensed setting, Free Tuition: 485 (10 pages). Paging with skip/take returned exactly the reported total of unique programs each time.
- Details and CCLD records for all 516 programs, 16 requests at a time, took 25.2 s with a cold cache (20.5 programs/s) and no failures.
- Jev (jev-1.13.0): about 160 ms per call; 6 concurrent calls finished in 236 ms without rate limiting; about 1,500 input and 125 output tokens per program. Scoring 250 programs is about 375k input tokens per search.

Where the limits live:
- src/recommendations.js: searchNearestFirst and searchAllPages (PROVIDER_BATCH_SIZE = 50, MAX_PAGES_PER_SEARCH = 6, and a one-page citywide fallback when fewer than MIN_NEARBY_RESULTS = 10 match nearby); JEV_MAX_SCORED = 25; PUBLIC_PROGRAM_LIMIT = 20 and the per-list caps.
- src/carewait-client.js: searchProfiles and getSiteDetails throw on any non-2xx response, with no retry; a failed detail lookup leaves only a lookupWarnings entry.
- src/ccld-client.js: getFacilityDetail turns any error into an "unavailable" record with no retry, which moves a healthy program into unverifiedSafetyCandidates. Only verified records are cached.
- src/jev-eval.js: 8 concurrent calls, SDK default of 2 retries with backoff, and a 60 s deadline for the whole scoring phase.
close_reason: All nine exhaustive-search tasks are complete and the live full-page checks passed.

title: Add secret scanning, SAST, and required merge checks
description: The new GitHub Actions pipeline runs tests and npm audit, but the repository still has no code-scanning or secret-detection workflow, and branch protection cannot be defined in Git files. The CCSF SDLC standard is a useful reference, though this project is not CCSF and has no hosted deployment target.
design: Add pinned, low-privilege source analysis and secret scanning to pull requests. Configure the main-branch ruleset to require the CI and security checks before merge. Keep dependency audit and Dependabot updates as implemented.
acceptance_criteria: Pull requests run JavaScript static analysis and secret scanning with no unreviewed high-confidence findings; main requires successful CI and security checks before merge; README accurately describes configured checks and platform-only settings.

title: Cache CareWait details and CCLD records per server process
description:
Every recommendation call refetches every program's CareWait details and every unverified CCLD record. Once each search covers every program (500+) and agents page through results, repeat work dominates. The MCP server is a long-lived process, so an in-memory cache pays off across calls.

Files: src/carewait-client.js (getSiteDetails), src/ccld-client.js (the cache map, which holds verified records only and never expires).
design:
- A small TTL cache (a Map with timestamps and a size cap) for getSiteDetails results, keyed by entityId, TTL about 6 hours.
- Give the CCLD cache the same TTL, and keep caching only verified records so failed lookups are retried.
- Deduplicate in-flight requests: concurrent callers for the same key share one promise.
- Allow turning the cache off (for example SFEL_CACHE=off) for debugging.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests: a second lookup within the TTL does not call fetch; after the TTL it refetches; two concurrent lookups make one request; failures are not cached.
- A repeated identical recommendation search in the same process makes no CareWait detail or CCLD requests.
close_reason: TTL caches, in-flight dedupe, bypass, and failure behavior implemented and tested.

title: Make Jev's budget rating track how far over budget a program is
description:
Jev's budget-fit ratings for over-budget programs do not track price. In a live search near 94102 (Half Credit, $1,200 budget), a program with a $1,322 net cost scored 0.08 while $1,647 programs scored 0.44 and 0.48 (out of 3). All fall in the rubric's lowest level ("Net monthly cost exceeds the budget"), so the rating within that level is noise, and it reorders the over-budget list, which is sorted by the composite.

File: src/jev-eval.js (the budgetFit rubric in buildQuestions).
design:
- Give the budget rubric levels that separate how far over budget a program is, for example: more than 50% over; 10% to 50% over; up to 10% over; within budget; $0 or well below. Alternatively, add the overage percentage to the state Jev sees.
- Keep budget fit a Jev judgment; do not replace it with a formula.
acceptance_criteria:
- Live: in the 94102 Half Credit $1,200 search, over-budget programs' budget ratings fall as net cost rises.
- Unit tests cover the new rubric.

title: Let agents send provider-website prices back for Jev scoring
description: Programs without a published CareWait rate are listed for tuition verification and never scored by Jev. The skill has the agent find prices on provider websites (SKILL.md Section 6), but those programs stay "Not scored (price from provider site)", because scoring happens inside get_smart_recommendations before the agent reads any page. Once every program is checked citywide (sfel-2qw), this list grows to hundreds of programs.
design:
- Add an optional verifiedPrices parameter to get_smart_recommendations: [{ entityId, grossMonthlyMin, grossMonthlyMax, sourceUrl, accessedDate }].
- The server applies the ELFA credit only when the provider's detail record lists the family's tier, marks the rate source as the provider site, has Jev score those programs with the others, and places them in recommendations or stretchOptions.
- Return sourceUrl and accessedDate with each program so the agent can cite them.
- Update SKILL.md Section 6: after finding prices, call get_smart_recommendations again with verifiedPrices.
acceptance_criteria: - Tests: a program with a verified price lands in a Jev-ranked list, with the credit applied only when the provider lists the family's tier; the source URL is returned; results without verifiedPrices are unchanged.
